claims.disproof_condition: Downgrade if the agreement is terminated/renegotiated below firm volumes, if JARE fails to take delivery at floor terms in subsequent quarterlies, or if HRE-free magnet adoption (Proterial NMX-HF watch already in graph) erodes the HRE half of the commitment's value.
claims.statement: Customer-side capital commitment for Lynas is now contractual and regulated-disclosure grade: JARE (JOGMEC+Sojitz SPV) firmly commits to purchase 5,000 tonnes NdPr per annum plus 50% of ALL Lynas HRE oxide output, with a US$110/kg NdPr floor price, upside sharing above US$150/kg, agreement to 2038, and an existing long-term senior loan facility. Money flows customer→supplier (financing + firm offtake with floor) — the strongest form of the four-dimension test's third axis. This upgrades the Lynas ex-China positioning from supplier self-report to counterparty-bound commitment.

source_doc.title: Lynas ASX announcement — Enhanced JARE Agreement for Japanese Industry

sources.quote: JARE will provide a firm commitment to purchase 5,000 tonnes NdPr per annum for Japanese industry with an agreed market-linked floor price

75% of all HRE oxides produced by Lynas will be made available to Japanese industry, with a firm commitment from JARE to purchase the equivalent of 50% of all HRE oxides produced by Lynas for Japanese industry

sources.locator: Announcement — floor price and upside sharing
sources.quote: Lynas and JARE have agreed a market-based offtake price with a price floor of US$110/kg NdPr for sales to Japanese industry and an upside sharing arrangement. Where Lynas’ achieved price is above US$150/kg NdPr, an amount equal to 30% of the upside above US$150/kg NdPr, capped at a maximum of US$10 million each calendar year, will be paid to JARE.

sources.locator: Footnote — JARE identity and loan facility
sources.quote: JARE is a special purpose company established by Japan Organization for Metals and Energy Security (JOGMEC) and Sojitz Corporation. Lynas and JARE are parties to a long term senior loan facility.
Lynas will provide up to 7,200 tonnes per annum of NdPr to Japanese industry to 2038
